name: Master of Cyber Security
description: This course builds the skills to defend networks, systems and data. Students work through lab exercises on attack and defence, then apply them in a final project with a real organisation. Later units let you lean towards either technical defence or security management.

name: Master of Cybersecurity
description: A two-year coursework degree for graduates from computing and related fields. You learn how attacks work by running them in a contained lab, and then learn to detect and stop them. The second year is taken up by an industry project and a short research report.

name: Master of Cyber Security and Privacy
description: Security and privacy are taught side by side, so graduates can design systems that protect data and respect the people it describes. Classes mix studio work, case studies from past breaches and short technical labs. Students finish with a project that fixes a real weakness in a working system.

name: Master of Cyber Security Operations
description: A one-year course for people who want to work in a security operations centre. You learn to read logs, hunt for intruders and write the playbooks a team follows when an alert fires. Most teaching happens on a simulated network that is attacked each week.

name: Master of Information Security
description: Covers the technical and organisational sides of protecting information. Students study cryptography, secure networks and access control, and also how a security program is run day to day. Assessment is mostly practical reports and a supervised dissertation.

name: Master of Cyber Security
description: Aimed at graduates who want to move into security from IT, engineering or science. The first year sets the technical base in networks, systems and programming for security. The second year is for specialist units and a placement or research project.

name: Master of Cybersecurity Engineering
description: An engineering-led degree about building systems that resist attack from the start. Students write code, harden operating systems and design network architectures, then test their own work against classmates. It suits people with a software or electronics background.

name: Master of Cyber Security (Advanced)
description: A one-year degree for graduates who already hold a computing qualification. It moves quickly through advanced attack techniques, defensive tooling and security architecture. Students complete one large practical assessment in place of a thesis.

name: Diploma of Information Technology (Cyber Security)
description: A hands-on diploma that teaches the basics of keeping computers and networks safe. You set up firewalls, manage user accounts, and learn to spot and report suspicious activity. Workplace tasks are built into most units.

name: Diploma of Network Security
description: Students learn how data travels across a network and where it can be intercepted or altered. Practical sessions cover configuring routers, switches, VPNs and monitoring tools. The course is built for people who want to work in network support with a security focus.

name: Diploma of Cloud and Infrastructure Security
description: A two-year diploma on protecting servers, storage and services that run in the cloud and in company data rooms. You practise configuring identity controls, backups and logging, and learn how to respond when something is misconfigured. Work placements are part of the second year.

name: Diploma of Applied Cyber Security
description: This diploma gives a practical start in security for people with little computing background. Short units on networks, passwords, malware and safe software habits build up to a small project defending a model office network. It can lead on to a degree.

name: Diploma of Security Operations Centre Analysis
description: Prepares students for the first line of a security team. You monitor alerts, sort real attacks from false alarms, and write clear tickets for the people who fix problems. Teaching uses recorded incidents and a live practice network.

name: Master of Penetration Testing and Ethical Hacking
description: Students are trained to break into systems with permission and report what they find. The course covers testing of networks, web applications and wireless links, plus the legal rules around testing. A final assessment is a full test against a prepared target with a written report.

name: Master of Applied Cryptography
description: A mathematically grounded course on how encryption and digital signatures really work and how they fail in practice. Students implement algorithms, break weak ones, and study how protocols are used inside real products. Suited to graduates with a strong maths or computing record.

name: Master of Cloud Security
description: Covers the way security is built into cloud services, from identity to container platforms. You work in real cloud accounts, writing policies as code and reading the logs that show an attack in progress. A short industry placement is available.

name: Master of Network Security
description: Goes deep on protecting communication networks, from enterprise setups to telecom links. Students design secure networks, test them for gaps and learn the protocols that keep traffic private. The second year includes a research project with a staff supervisor.

name: Master of Secure Software Engineering
description: Teaches software developers to write code that is hard to attack. Units follow the path of a program from requirements to release, with code review, testing tools and threat modelling at each step. Students build and defend a small application throughout.

name: Master of Cyber Defence
description: A one-year course about stopping attackers once they are already inside. Students practise detection, containment and recovery on a simulated company network with a red team working against them. Teamwork and clear communication are marked as well as technical results.

name: Diploma of Cyber Security Fundamentals
description: An entry diploma that explains how attacks happen and how everyday protections work. Students use common tools to scan, lock down and monitor a home or small business setup. No earlier computing study is assumed.

name: Diploma of Ethical Hacking
description: Learn how attackers think by doing what they do, in a safe lab and within the law. The course moves from scanning and password attacks to simple web exploits and report writing. It is a practical first step before a degree in security.

name: Master of Cyber Security Analytics
description: Combines data skills with security work. Students learn to collect large volumes of logs and network records, find patterns that point to an attack, and build models that flag unusual behaviour. Programming in Python is used throughout.

name: Master of Application Security
description: Focused on web, mobile and desktop applications and the flaws that put them at risk. You learn to test code, review designs and fix problems before release. A placement with a development team is encouraged in the final term.

name: Diploma of Digital Security Administration
description: For people who run the day-to-day security of an office or small organisation. The course teaches account management, patching, backups and the monitoring tools used to see what is going on. Students spend time in a work setting applying what they learn.

name: Master of Blockchain and Distributed Ledger Security
description: Looks at how blockchains and smart contracts are attacked and how to build them safely. Students read and audit contract code, study consensus weaknesses and analyse real cases of stolen funds. A good fit for graduates with programming experience.

name: Diploma of Cyber Threat Intelligence
description: Students learn to collect and make sense of information about attackers and their methods. The work includes tracking campaigns, writing short intelligence reports and sharing findings with a team. Case studies from public incident write-ups are used throughout.

name: Master of Threat Intelligence and Incident Response
description: A degree that follows an incident from the first warning through to the lessons learned afterwards. Students study how threat groups operate, practise running a response, and write the reports that senior staff read. The second year is a placement or an extended research project.

name: Master of Mobile and Embedded Security
description: Concentrates on phones, vehicles, medical devices and other small computers that are hard to patch. Students take devices apart in software, study their firmware and learn how to defend them. Hardware labs are used in most weeks.

name: Diploma of Cyber Security Operations
description: A two-year diploma that moves from basic networking to running security tools in a working team. Students keep a log of tasks done in real or simulated workplaces, and finish by handling a staged incident from start to end. Suits people returning to study or changing careers.

name: Master of Internet of Things Security
description: Connected sensors, cameras and appliances are the subject here. Students learn how these devices talk to each other and to the cloud, where they leak data, and how to lock them down. Projects involve building and attacking a small device network.

name: Diploma of Cloud Security Support
description: Gives a working start in looking after cloud accounts safely. Students set up users and permissions, turn on logging, and check settings against a simple checklist. Practical work is done in a training cloud environment.

name: Master of Security Operations and Automation
description: A short degree for people who want to reduce the manual work in security teams. You write scripts that collect evidence, enrich alerts and close routine cases. Students also learn when automation should be switched off and a person should step in.

name: Diploma of Secure Web Development
description: For web developers who want to stop common attacks in the sites they build. Units cover input handling, sessions, passwords and safe use of third-party code. Each week you break a small site, then repair it.

name: Master of Information Security Governance
description: This course looks at how organisations decide what to protect and how much to spend doing it. Students write security policies, assess risks and present options to managers. It is suited to those heading toward a security manager role rather than hands-on technical work.

name: Master of Cyber Risk and Compliance
description: Teaches how to find, rank and report cyber risk in a way that boards and regulators can act on. The units draw on common frameworks and past enforcement cases. Students prepare a risk register and audit report for a case organisation as their main assessment.

name: Master of Privacy and Data Protection
description: Explains the law and practice of handling personal data. You review how data flows through a company, assess the harm if it leaks, and write the notices and procedures that follow. Classes use case studies and short drafting exercises.

name: Diploma of Security Risk Management
description: A practical diploma on spotting risks to information and the people who use it. You learn to fill in a risk register, check that controls are working and write up findings plainly. Workplace tasks are included in each unit.

name: Master of Information Assurance
description: A degree about proving that information is accurate, available and kept private. Students study standards, audit methods and the design of controls, then apply them to a live case. The second year includes a dissertation on an assurance question of their choice.

name: Master of Cyber Security Management
description: Made for professionals stepping into a security leadership role. The course is about budgets, staff, vendors and the plans a team follows when things go wrong. Students practise through simulated board briefings and tabletop exercises, with an optional placement.

name: Diploma of Governance, Risk and Compliance
description: Introduces how organisations keep to rules and standards for information. Students build a simple compliance plan, check it with an audit checklist and report gaps. Suits administrators and junior staff in regulated fields.

name: Master of IT Audit and Assurance
description: Prepares graduates to review computer systems and judge whether they can be trusted. Teaching covers audit planning, testing of controls and the writing of clear findings. Students work with sample company data sets to practise each stage.

name: Master of Digital Forensics
description: Students learn to find, preserve and examine digital evidence from computers, phones and networks. Practical work follows the same steps used in a lawful investigation, from imaging a drive to giving evidence in a mock hearing. Placements with investigation teams are offered in the second year.

name: Master of Digital Forensics and Incident Response
description: Brings together evidence work and live response. You learn to collect data from a running machine, work out what an intruder did and write a report that stands up to challenge. The course is intense and mostly lab based.

name: Diploma of Digital Forensics
description: An introduction to recovering and recording digital evidence. Students practise with write blockers, imaging tools and basic file recovery, and keep careful notes as an investigator would. It builds toward further study in forensic computing.

name: Master of Cyber Crime Investigation
description: Looks at online crime from the investigator side, including fraud, harassment and data theft. Students study how offenders hide, how traces are followed across services and how cases are put together for court. The course blends computing, criminology and law.

name: Master of Mobile and Cloud Forensics
description: Covers the hard cases: locked phones, encrypted apps and data that lives on servers somewhere else. Students learn the tools and the limits of each method, and how to explain uncertainty in a report. Lab time is high and written work is short and precise.

name: Diploma of Digital Evidence Handling
description: A short practical diploma for people who need to collect and store digital evidence correctly. You learn chain of custody, how to copy data without changing it and how to record what you did. Work experience is built into the course.

name: Master of Forensic Computing
description: A research-aware degree in the science behind forensic tools. Students test how reliable the methods are, study file systems and operating system traces in depth, and write a thesis on a forensic problem. Suitable for those thinking of research or laboratory roles.

name: Master of Malware Analysis and Reverse Engineering
description: Teaches how to take apart harmful software and explain what it does. You read assembly, watch programs run in a sandbox and write detection rules from what you find. Assessments are analysis reports on supplied samples.

name: Master of Cyber Psychology
description: This course asks why people click, share and trust online, and what that means for safety. Students learn psychology research methods and apply them to scams, misinformation and risky behaviour. It suits graduates from psychology, security or the social sciences.

name: Master of Cyber Behaviour and Human Factors
description: Explores the human side of security, from badly designed warnings to staff who are pressured into mistakes. Students run small studies with real users and propose changes to systems or training. Placements with security teams are available in the second year.

name: Master of Social Engineering and Human Risk
description: Studies how attackers manipulate people and how organisations can reduce the chance of it working. You analyse real phishing and phone scams, design test campaigns within ethics rules and measure what changes behaviour. A one-year course with plenty of discussion.

name: Diploma of Security Awareness and Behaviour
description: Helps students build short training that people actually remember. You learn how habits form, why warnings get ignored and how to write clear messages for staff. A small awareness campaign is designed and tested as the final task.

name: Master of Online Behaviour and Digital Wellbeing
description: Examines how time online shapes mood, relationships and risk, with attention to young people and vulnerable users. Students learn clinical and social research methods and look at the design choices that make platforms hard to put down. The final year is a placement or a supervised study.

name: Master of Human-Centred Security
description: Brings design thinking to security so tools suit the people who use them. Students observe users, prototype safer interfaces and test whether they work. Projects are done in small teams with a client brief.

name: Diploma of Online Safety and Digital Behaviour
description: Prepares people who support others in staying safe online, such as in schools, libraries and community groups. The course covers scams, bullying and privacy, and how to talk about them without blame. Placements in community settings are part of the program.

name: Master of Industrial Control Systems Security
description: Industrial control systems run factories, water plants and power networks, and they are built differently from office networks. Students learn their protocols, their weak points and how to defend them without stopping production. A test bench of real controllers is used for lab work.

name: Master of Critical Infrastructure Protection
description: Covers the protection of energy, water, transport and communications systems. Students study how these systems depend on each other, what regulators expect and how an attack could spread. Assessment includes a resilience plan for a case network.

name: Diploma of Industrial Cyber Security
description: A practical diploma for technicians who work near plant and machine controls. You learn what is different about securing equipment that cannot be switched off for updates. Training is hands-on with controllers and industrial networking gear.

name: Master of OT and SCADA Security
description: Focuses on supervisory control and data acquisition systems used by utilities and mining operations. Students learn how to map a control network, find hidden connections to the office side and plan upgrades that keep operations running. The second year is for a project with an industrial partner.

name: Master of Cyber-Physical Systems Security
description: Looks at systems where software controls physical machinery, such as robots, vehicles and building controls. Students model how an attack on the software can cause physical effects and design checks to catch it. Laboratory work uses small robots and control rigs.

name: Diploma of Industrial Automation Security
description: Two years on how automated production lines are programmed and how they can be protected. The first year teaches controllers and networks, and the second adds security testing, monitoring and a work placement. Suits apprentices and technicians.

name: Master of Smart Grid and Utilities Cyber Security
description: A one-year degree on the digital side of electricity and water networks. Students look at smart meters, substations and remote control links, and learn to assess and reduce the risks in each. A case study on a regional utility runs through the course.

name: Master of Maritime and Transport Cyber Security
description: Treats ships, ports, rail and aviation systems as targets that need their own security thinking. Students study navigation and signalling systems, their known flaws and the rules that apply to operators. Teaching uses incident reports and a simulation of a port network.

name: Master of Cyber Strategy and Policy
description: Explores how governments and large organisations plan for cyber threats. Students read policy papers, compare national approaches and write their own briefing papers. Debate and short presentations are used as much as essays.

name: Master of Cyber Conflict and National Security
description: Examines how states use cyber operations in rivalry and conflict, and how defence and intelligence agencies respond. The course combines security studies with enough technical content to judge claims about attacks. Students complete a research thesis in the second year.

name: Master of Cyber Law and Policy
description: A law-oriented degree on the rules that govern data, networks and online harm. Students study privacy, criminal law, jurisdiction and international agreements, and learn how policy is drafted. Moot discussions and drafting exercises replace many exams.

name: Master of Cyber Diplomacy and International Security
description: Looks at how countries negotiate rules for behaviour online and manage incidents that cross borders. Students analyse treaties, regional agreements and recent disputes, and role-play negotiations. A short course for those heading toward policy and public service.

name: Master of Strategic Cyber Leadership
description: Prepares experienced professionals to guide an organisation through a cyber crisis and to plan years ahead. Units cover board advice, strategy under uncertainty and managing public communication after a breach. A placement or mentoring project is part of the course.

name: Diploma of Cyber Policy Foundations
description: A first look at how cyber issues become laws, rules and national plans. Students read short policy documents, learn who the main actors are and practise writing a one-page brief. No technical background is needed.

name: Master of Cyber Security Leadership
description: Designed for senior technical staff moving into direction-setting roles. The course covers security strategy, working with executives and building a team culture that supports good practice. Assessment is based on strategy documents for a case company.

name: Diploma of Cyber Security Strategy
description: Gives managers and technical staff a plain-language view of cyber planning. Students learn to set goals, rank threats and explain trade-offs to non-specialists. The final task is a short strategy for a small organisation.

name: Master of Defence and Cyber Operations Strategy
description: A degree on how military and civil agencies plan, authorise and limit operations in cyberspace. Students study doctrine, law and ethics, then work through planning exercises with realistic constraints. Suited to those from defence, policing or public administration.
